svg.title: Correlating scheduler wakeup and switch events
svg.desc: A trace timeline correlates sched_wakeup for one task with the next sched_switch naming it as next, yielding runnable latency. Unknown intervals and conditions remain explicit, and unavailable tracing is recorded as SKIP.
svg.text: Day 7 evidence: correlate events, preserve unknowns
ordered trace for TID 4242
sched_wakeup
state is TASK_RUNNING
sched_switch
next = TID 4242
correlated runnable latency
SUPPORTED INTERPRETATION
✓ this task became runnable at wakeup event
✓ this task was named next at switch event
✓ interval is event-to-event for one TID
✓ CPU/event order can test hypotheses
✓ source maps event sites for pinned commit
UNKNOWN / NOT IMPLIED
? time before kernel wakeup
? time from switch to userspace work
? exact policy reason for the choice
? every lock, branch, or competing task
? host/source version equivalence
If trace access or tools are unavailable: SKIP + reason
Use read-only baseline counters as aggregates; do not convert source tracepoints into synthetic output.
SKIP is evidence about the environment, not a failed scheduler mechanism.
